gloss: Honorific address on an adult male; mister, sir
glosses: Honorific address on an adult male; mister, sir
etym: Via Volga Turki, from Ottoman Turkish افندی (efendi) (compare modern Turkish efendi, also possibly mediated by Arabic أَفَنْدِي (ʔafandī)), from Greek αφέντη (afénti), vocative of αφέντης (aféntis), from Ancient Greek αὐθέντης (authéntēs, “

From
Persian رحمت (rahmat, “mercy”),
from
Arabic رَحْمَة (raḥma, “compassion, mercy”).
Apparently, a Central Asian innovative use in the sense of "thank you".
Compare to Tatar рәхмәт (räxmät), Kazakh рахмет (raxmet)/рақмет (raqmet), Kyrgyz

Cognate with
Tatar аркасында (arqasında, “because of, thanks to”),
Kazakh арқасында (arqasında, “thanks to”),
Uzbek orqasida (“because of, thanks to”),
etc.
